rationale: Evidence: iteration 6 (kp 2.25, kd 1.2, base 1.2, 16 mm sensors at x = ±0.03 m, mass 0.6 kg, body 0.14 m) is the best design at 909.8. Its oval (20/20, 2.05 s) and s-bend (20/20, 2.38 s) are solid. The slalom is the remaining gap: 16/20 finishes, 4 off-track exits, 0.2 line-loss events per run, rms 0.012 m, steering oscillation 0.26. Two single-variable tests bracket the current point. Raising kd to 1.5 (iteration 8) gave no gain (907.6) and raised control effort, so derivative damping is saturated. Lowering kp to 2.0 (iteration 7) hurt, with slalom finishes falling to 11/20 and line-loss events rising to 0.6. That points to too little turn authority on the tightest bends, not too much gain. Change: raise kp from 2.25 to 2.5 with kd held at 1.2, ki 0, and every geometry value unchanged. The extra proportional authority should keep the robot on the tape through sharp slalom bends and cut line-loss events. Steering oscillation has headroom (about 0.26 against a limit near 0.35), so the risk of jitter is moderate. Expected result: slalom finish rate 0.85 or higher, slalom mean above 850, line_loss_events on the slalom at or below 0.2, and oval and s-bend close to iteration 6. Hypotheses: (H1) the slalom failures come from insufficient turn authority, so kp 2.5 reduces them; (H2) if steering_oscillation rises above 0.35 or control_effort jumps, kp has reached its useful limit and the next step is kp 2.25 with ki 0.1 to address drift; (H3) if line_loss_events on the slalom stay near 0.2 regardless of kp, the cause is the sensor footprint and the next change should be to a 12 mm sensor layout or a wider spread. Measurements wanted per track: completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation, control_effort and noise_robustness, to separate line loss from overshoot.
